sheets.title: Stone and metal ages
sheets.intro: Each age: when, tools, sites and the first thing it gave us.

keys.name: Lower Palaeolithic

rows.v: Sohan (pebble choppers, NW Punjab); Acheulian / Madrasian (hand-axes, South)
Attirampakkam (TN, ~1.5 mn yrs), Pallavaram (Madras – first find, Robert Bruce Foote 1863), Isampur (Karnataka), Hunsgi, Didwana, Bhimbetka
Food gatherers, hunters; no fire control early

traps: Pallavaram (first find, 1863) ≠ Attirampakkam (oldest date, 1.5 mn years)

rows.v: Nevasa (Pravara river, Maharashtra – "Nevasian"), Luni valley, Bhimbetka, Narmada valley
Hathnora (Narmada) gave India's oldest hominid skull (Homo erectus/archaic sapiens)

keys.name: Upper Palaeolithic

rows.v: Bhimbetka (MP, rock shelters, oldest rock art), Belan valley (UP), Kurnool caves (AP – bone tools)
Homo sapiens; ostrich-egg shell beads (Patne, Maharashtra)

traps: Bhimbetka is a UNESCO site (2003), shelters span Palaeolithic to Medieval

keys.name: Mesolithic

rows.v: Animal domestication (dog first); burials with goods
Bagor (Rajasthan – largest site, earliest animal domestication), Adamgarh (MP – domestication), Langhnaj (Gujarat), Sarai Nahar Rai, Mahadaha, Damdama (UP – burials), Bhimbetka (paintings)

traps: Bagor and Adamgarh = earliest domestication (Mesolithic), not Neolithic

keys.name: Neolithic

rows.v: Polished stone axes (celts); pottery; first farming
Earliest farming – wheat, barley; cattle, sheep, goat; mud-brick houses
Pit dwellings; dog buried with master; bone tools
Utnur (Mahbubnagar – ash mound), Nagarjunakonda, Ramapuram, Palavoy, Singanapalli
Corded pottery; links to SE Asia

traps: Burzahom – dog buried with man; Gufkral – potter’s cave
Mehrgarh = earliest farming; Koldihwa = earliest rice

keys.name: Chalcolithic

rows.v: Ahar-Banas (Rajasthan – Gilund), Kayatha (MP), Malwa (Navdatoli), Jorwe (Maharashtra – Inamgaon, Daimabad, Nevasa)
Painted pottery – Black-and-Red Ware; first villages of peninsula
Large village; urn burials under house floors; fortified
Bronze chariot, rhinoceros, elephant, buffalo figures

traps: Daimabad bronzes are Late Harappan / Chalcolithic, not Harappan core

rows.v: c. 1200 BCE onward (PGW in Ganga plain c. 1100 BCE)
Painted Grey Ware (PGW) = Later Vedic; NBPW (c. 700 BCE) = Mahajanapadas
Burials marked by big stones – cists, dolmens, menhirs; Black-and-Red Ware
Brahmagiri (Karnataka), Adichanallur (TN, urn burials), Hallur (Karnataka – early iron)

sheets.title: Indus Valley sites
sheets.intro: Site, river, who dug it, and the find that gets asked.

keys.name: Harappan civilisation

rows.v: Harappa 1921 (Daya Ram Sahni), Mohenjo-daro 1922 (R.D. Banerji); John Marshall was ASI head
About 1,500 sites; Manda (J&K) north, Daimabad (Maharashtra) south, Sutkagendor (Baluchistan) west, Alamgirpur (UP) east
Grid streets, covered drains, citadel (west) + lower town (east); burnt bricks 1:2:4
Wheat, barley; first cotton ("sindon"); trade with Mesopotamia ("Meluhha")
Steatite, square; unicorn most common; script boustrophedon, undeciphered
Mother goddess, Pashupati seal, fire altars; no temples found

traps: Largest Indian site = Rakhigarhi (Haryana), not Dholavira
Most common seal animal = unicorn; no horse, no lion (lion absent)

rows.v: Two rows of granaries (6 each), working floors, R-37 cemetery, coffin burial, stone torso (red sandstone)
Indus river, Larkana, Sindh (Pak); "Mound of the dead"
Great Bath, Great Granary, assembly hall, bronze dancing girl, bearded priest (steatite), Pashupati seal, woven cotton
Dockyard (world's oldest), bead factory, fire altars, rice husk, Persian Gulf seal, double burial, chess-like game, ivory scale

keys.name: Kalibangan

rows.v: A. Ghosh 1953; B.B. Lal, B.K. Thapar
Ploughed field (pre-Harappan, criss-cross furrows), fire altars, earthquake trace, wooden drain

traps: Ploughed field = Kalibangan; terracotta plough = Banawali

rows.v: Khadir island, Rann of Kutch, Gujarat
Three-part town, signboard of 10 big letters, water reservoirs and stadium; UNESCO site 2021
No citadel; bead making; ink pot; dog chasing cat footprint
Largest Harappan site in India; DNA study 2019
Dog buried with master; first site dug after Independence (Y.D. Sharma 1953)

keys.name: Decline theories
traps: Wheeler = Aryan invasion; Marshall = first big survey

sheets.title: Vedic age
sheets.intro: Each text: books, gods, priest; rivers by old names.

keys.name: Rig Veda

rows.v: Mandalas 2 – 7 ("family books": Gritsamada, Vishvamitra, Vamadeva, Atri, Bharadvaja, Vasishtha)
Mandalas 1, 8, 9, 10; 9th = Soma hymns; 10th = Purusha Sukta (4 varnas), Nasadiya Sukta (creation)
Indra (250 hymns), Agni (200), Varuna (rita, cosmic order), Soma, Mitra, Rudra; goddesses Ushas, Aditi

traps: Purusha Sukta (varnas) is in the 10th mandala, a late addition
Gayatri: Mandala 3, Vishvamitra

rows.v: Hymns set to tune; most taken from Rig Veda
Shukla (white – Vajasaneyi Samhita) and Krishna (black – Taittiriya)

keys.name: Atharva Veda

rows.v: Charms, spells, cures, magic; daily life
Calls Sabha and Samiti "twin daughters of Prajapati"

traps: Sabha and Samiti as "twin daughters" = Atharva Veda

keys.name: Later Vedic texts

rows.v: Rituals explained – Aitareya (Rig), Shatapatha (Yajur – longest; tells Videgha Mathava spreading Agni east)
108; philosophy (atman, brahman); Vedanta. Mundaka – "Satyameva Jayate"; Chandogya – first 3 ashramas, Svetaketu; Katha – Nachiketa and Yama
Six – Shiksha (phonetics), Kalpa (ritual), Vyakarana (grammar), Nirukta (etymology), Chhanda (metre), Jyotisha (astronomy)

traps: "Satyameva Jayate" – Mundaka Upanishad
Jabala Upanishad mentions all 4 ashramas

keys.name: Rig Vedic rivers
traps: Parushni = Ravi (Dasarajna); Asikni = Chenab

keys.name: Early vs Later Vedic

rows.v: Early – Sapta Sindhu (Punjab); Later – Ganga-Yamuna doab, Kosala, Videha
Early – cattle (gavishti = war for cows); Later – farming, iron (krishna ayas), PGW pottery
Early – tribal; rajan elected-ish; Sabha, Samiti, Vidatha; Later – bigger kingdoms, Rajasuya, Ashvamedha, Vajapeya
Early – varna loose, women in assemblies (Apala, Ghosha, Lopamudra); Later – rigid varna, women fall
Early – Indra, Agni; Later – Prajapati, Vishnu, Rudra

traps: Battle of Ten Kings (Dasarajna): Sudas (Bharata) won on the Parushni

keys.name: Mahavira

rows.v: Father Siddhartha (Jnatrika); mother Trishala (Lichchhavi, sister of Chetaka); wife Yashoda; daughter Anojja (Priyadarshana)
Left home at 30; Kaivalya at 42 (sal tree, Jrimbhikagrama, river Rijupalika); died 72 at Pavapuri
5 vows (added Brahmacharya to Parshva's 4); Triratna; Anekantavada, Syadvada
11 Ganadharas; first Indrabhuti Gautama; Sudharma survived

traps: Yashoda = Mahavira’s wife; Yashodhara = Buddha’s wife
Parshvanatha (23rd) gave 4 vows; Mahavira added the 5th

rows.v: 512 CE, Vallabhi, Devardhi Kshamashramana – canon written
12-year famine (Chandragupta Maurya); Bhadrabahu went south → Digambara; Sthulabhadra stayed → Svetambara
Sky-clad; women need rebirth as men
Chandragupta Maurya, Kharavela (Hathigumpha), Amoghavarsha I, Kumarapala (Hemachandra)
Shravanabelagola (Gomateshwara 981, Chamundaraya), Dilwara (1031), Palitana, Sammed Shikhar

keys.name: Gautama Buddha

rows.v: Father Suddhodana; mother Mahamaya (died); raised by Prajapati Gautami; wife Yashodhara; son Rahula
Old man, sick man, dead body, ascetic
Mahabhinishkramana (left home, 29) – horse; Nirvana at Bodh Gaya (35) – Bodhi tree; first sermon Sarnath (Dharmachakrapravartana) – wheel; Mahaparinirvana at Kushinagar (80) – stupa
4 Noble Truths; 8-fold path; Middle Path; no soul, no god

traps: First sermon = Sarnath (deer park), not Bodh Gaya

keys.name: Buddhist councils

rows.v: 483 BCE, Rajagriha (Saptaparni cave); Ajatashatru; Mahakassapa – Sutta and Vinaya Pitaka (Ananda, Upali)
383 BCE, Vaishali; Kalashoka; Sabakami – split Sthaviravadin vs Mahasanghika
250 BCE, Pataliputra; Ashoka; Moggaliputta Tissa – Abhidhamma Pitaka; missions sent
c. 72 CE (1st century CE), Kundalvana, Kashmir; Kanishka; Vasumitra (Ashvaghosha vice) – Mahayana vs Hinayana; Mahavibhasha in Sanskrit

traps: Abhidhamma added at 3rd council; Mahayana split at 4th

keys.name: Buddhist schools and texts

rows.v: Theravada; Buddha as teacher; Pali; Sri Lanka, Myanmar
Bodhisattva; idol worship; Sanskrit; Nagarjuna (Madhyamika, Shunyavada) – Andhra
Tripitaka (Vinaya – rules, Sutta – sermons, Abhidhamma – philosophy); Jatakas (past lives); Milindapanho (Menander + Nagasena); Dipavamsa, Mahavamsa (Sri Lanka); Buddhacharita (Ashvaghosha)
Sanchi (Ashoka), Amaravati, Nagarjunakonda, Nalanda, Vikramashila, Ajanta

traps: Nagarjuna (Madhyamika) is linked to Nagarjunakonda, Andhra

keys.name: Ajivikas and others

rows.v: Makkhali Gosala; fate (niyati) rules all; Barabar caves gifted by Ashoka and Dasharatha

traps: Barabar caves = Ajivikas, not Jains or Buddhists

rows.v: Kosaladevi (Kosala – Kashi as dowry), Chellana (Lichchhavi), Khema (Madra)
First Magadha king with a standing army; doctor Jivaka sent to Avanti's Pradyota
Beat Kosala (Prasenajit); 16-year war with Vajji (Lichchhavi) – used rathamusala (chariot-mace) and mahashilakantaka (catapult); minister Vassakara sowed split
2nd Buddhist council at Vaishali 383 BCE; capital back to Pataliputra

keys.name: Nandas

rows.v: Huge army and wealth; Alexander's troops refused to face him at the Beas (326 BCE)

traps: Alexander came during Dhana Nanda’s rule

rows.v: Hydaspes (Jhelum) 326 BCE vs Porus; won but restored him
Routes West – East opened; Greek satraps; Seleucus later fought Chandragupta

keys.name: Chandragupta Maurya

rows.v: Beat Seleucus Nicator 305 BCE – got Arachosia, Gedrosia, Paropamisadae, Aria; gave 500 elephants; marriage alliance
Sudarshana lake (Girnar) by governor Pushyagupta (Junagadh inscription of Rudradaman)
Jain; went south with Bhadrabahu; Sallekhana at Shravanabelagola (Chandragiri hill)

traps: Sudarshana lake: built under Chandragupta, repaired by Rudradaman and Skandagupta

rows.v: Deimachus (Seleucid, Antiochus I); Dionysius (Ptolemy II, Egypt)
Asked Antiochus for wine, figs and a sophist

keys.name: Ashoka

rows.v: Devanampiya Piyadasi; "Ashoka" name in Maski, Gujarra, Nittur, Udegolam edicts
Kalinga 261 BCE (8th year) – 1 lakh killed (Rock Edict XIII)
Dhamma Mahamatras (13th year); tolerance, non-violence; Rajjukas, Pradesikas
14 Major Rock Edicts, 7 Pillar Edicts; Brahmi (mostly), Kharosthi (Shahbazgarhi, Mansehra), Greek & Aramaic (Kandahar); deciphered by James Prinsep 1837
Buddhist (Upagupta / Nigrodha); 3rd council 250 BCE; missions – son Mahendra & daughter Sanghamitra to Sri Lanka
Sanchi stupa, Sarnath lion capital (national emblem), Barabar caves (Ajivikas)
Amaravati, Erragudi (Kurnool) rock edicts, Rajula Mandagiri

traps: Rock Edict XIII = Kalinga war; RE XII = religious tolerance
Lion capital is from Sarnath, not Sanchi

keys.name: Mauryan state

rows.v: Sannidhata (treasury), Samaharta (revenue), Sitadhyaksha (crown land), Panyadhyaksha (trade), Sulkadhyaksha (customs)
Taxila (north), Ujjain (west), Tosali (Kalinga), Suvarnagiri (south), Pataliputra (centre); princes = Kumaras
Megasthenes – 6 boards of 5 members at Pataliputra

traps: Samaharta = revenue chief; Sannidhata = treasurer

rows.v: Brihadratha, killed by general Pushyamitra Shunga 185 BCE
185 BCE, during an army parade (Banabhatta, Harshacharita)
Ashoka's pacifism (H.P. Shastri – Brahmin reaction), weak heirs, split empire, costly bureaucracy (Kosambi), Greek attacks

sheets.title: After the Mauryas (200 BCE – 300 CE)
sheets.intro: Northern dynasties that filled the Mauryan gap.

keys.name: Pushyamitra Shunga

rows.v: Fought Indo-Greeks (Menander? per Patanjali, Malavikagnimitram); Kharavela of Kalinga attacked
Divyavadana calls him a persecutor of Buddhists; Malavikagnimitram (Kalidasa) – son Agnimitra

traps: Patanjali (Mahabhashya) was Pushyamitra’s priest

keys.name: Later Shungas and Kanvas

rows.v: Shunga; Greek envoy Heliodorus (from Antialcidas, Taxila) set up Garuda pillar at Besnagar (Vidisha) – first Vaishnava record by a Greek
Last Shunga; killed by minister Vasudeva Kanva c. 73 BCE
73 – 28 BCE; ended by Satavahanas (Simuka per Puranas)

traps: Heliodorus pillar = Besnagar, under Bhagabhadra

keys.name: Kharavela

rows.v: Raided Magadha, brought back Jina idol taken by Nandas; fought Satakarni; south up to Pandyas
Hathigumpha inscription (Udayagiri, Bhubaneswar) – year-by-year record, in Prakrit

traps: Hathigumpha = Kharavela; Junagadh = Rudradaman; Nasik = Gautami Balasri

keys.name: Indo-Greeks

rows.v: First to enter India c. 190 BCE
c. 165 – 130 BCE; capital Sakala (Sialkot); Buddhist; dialogue with Nagasena – Milindapanho
First with king portraits and inscriptions; first gold coins in India; bilingual (Greek + Kharosthi)

traps: First gold coins = Indo-Greeks; most gold coins = Kushanas; purest = Guptas

keys.name: Shakas

rows.v: Taxila, Mathura, Nasik (Kshaharata – Nahapana), Ujjain (Kardamaka – Chashtana), Kabul
57 BCE – said to mark a Malwa king driving out Shakas
c. 130 – 150 CE; Junagadh (Girnar) inscription 150 CE – first long Sanskrit inscription; repaired Sudarshana lake; beat Satavahana Pulumavi twice
78 CE (linked with Kanishka); India's national calendar

traps: Saka era 78 CE is India’s official calendar; Vikram Samvat 57 BCE

rows.v: St Thomas came to his court (Christian tradition)

keys.name: Kushanas

rows.v: Many gold coins; Shiva on coins
78 – 101 CE (78 = Saka era start); capitals Purushapura (Peshawar) and Mathura
Ashvaghosha (Buddhacharita), Vasumitra, Nagarjuna, Parshva, Charaka (physician), Mathara
4th Buddhist council (Kashmir); Mahayana patron; Peshawar stupa (Agesilaus)
Held Central Asia to Bengal – Silk Road trade
Gandhara (Greek style, grey schist) and Mathura (red sandstone) schools
Most gold coins; Buddha on coins
Vasudeva I, last big king (Shiva worshipper)

traps: Charaka = Kanishka’s court; Sushruta is earlier (surgery)

keys.name: Satavahanas

rows.v: Aharas (districts) under Amatyas; Mahasenapati, Mahabhoja; villages = gama
Land grants to Brahmins and Buddhists, tax-free
Lead, potin, copper; ship-mast coins (sea trade)
Kalyan, Sopara, Broach (west); Ghantasala, Motupalli, Kodur (east)
Amaravati stupa; Karle chaitya, Nasik, Kanheri caves; Bhattiprolu stupa

traps: Satavahana official language = Prakrit, not Telugu

rows.v: Beat Nahapana; restruck his coins (Jogalthembi hoard); "destroyer of Shakas, Yavanas, Pahlavas"
Nasik inscription of mother Gautami Balasri
Gatha Saptasati (Gaha Sattasai) – 700 love verses in Maharashtri Prakrit
Ptolemy names him "Siro Polemaios" of Baithana
Nagarjuna's Suhrillekha (letter to a Satavahana king) is linked to him by tradition

keys.name: Sangam age

rows.v: 1st Madurai (Agastya – lost), 2nd Kapadapuram (Tolkappiyam survives), 3rd Madurai (Nakkirar – most texts survive); Pandya patrons
Tolkappiyam (grammar, Tolkappiyar), Ettutogai (8 anthologies), Pattuppattu (10 idylls), Tirukkural (Tiruvalluvar – ethics, "Tamil Veda")
Silappadikaram (Ilango Adigal – Kannagi, Kovalan), Manimekalai (Sittalai Sattanar – Buddhist)

traps: Silappadikaram and Manimekalai = "twin epics", after the Sangam

keys.name: Sangam kingdoms

rows.v: Kerala; Vanji/Karur; port Muziris; emblem bow; Senguttuvan – Kannagi (Pattini) cult
Uraiyur, Puhar (Kaveripattinam); emblem tiger; Karikala – Kallanai (Grand Anicut) on Kaveri, battle of Venni
Madurai, port Korkai; emblem fish; Nedunjeliyan – Talaiyalanganam battle; pearls
Pepper, pearls, muslin to Rome – Arikamedu (Pondicherry) Roman goods; Periplus of the Erythraean Sea

traps: Karikala Chola = Kallanai; Senguttuvan Chera = Pattini cult

keys.name: Samudragupta

rows.v: North – "uprooted" 9 kings (Aryavarta); South – beat 12 kings, released them (Dharmavijaya): Vishnugopa of Kanchi, Hastivarman of Vengi, Kubera of Devarashtra, Mantaraja of Kurala
Vaishnava; let Meghavarna (Sri Lanka) build a monastery at Bodh Gaya

traps: Allahabad pillar: Ashoka edict + Harisena prashasti + Jahangir record
Hastivarman of Vengi = Salankayana, Andhra

keys.name: Chandragupta II Vikramaditya

rows.v: Ended Western Shakas (Rudrasimha III) – got Gujarat ports; Mehrauli iron pillar (Chandra) – Bengal, Vahlikas
Daughter Prabhavati married Vakataka Rudrasena II
First silver coins of Guptas; lion-slayer type
Navaratnas – Kalidasa, Amarasimha (Amarakosha), Varahamihira (by tradition), Dhanvantari, Vetala Bhatta…

traps: Fa-Hien came under Chandragupta II; Hiuen Tsang under Harsha
Iron pillar Mehrauli (Delhi) – no rust

keys.name: Gupta state and culture

rows.v: Bhukti (province, Uparika) → Vishaya (district, Vishayapati) → Grama; land grants (agrahara)
Aryabhata (Aryabhatiya, 499 – zero, π, earth rotates), Varahamihira (Brihat Samhita, Pancha Siddhantika), Brahmagupta (later), Vagbhata (medicine)
Kalidasa (Abhijnana Shakuntalam, Meghaduta, Raghuvamsha, Kumarasambhava, Malavikagnimitram); Shudraka (Mricchakatika); Vishakhadatta (Mudrarakshasa, Devichandraguptam); Vishnu Sharma (Panchatantra)
Deogarh Dashavatara temple (first shikhara), Bhitargaon brick temple, Sanchi temple 17, Ajanta caves 16, 17, 19; Sarnath Buddha

traps: Kalidasa wrote Malavikagnimitram, not Mudrarakshasa

keys.name: Harshavardhana

rows.v: Took Kannauj after Grahavarman's killing; lost to Pulakeshin II on the Narmada (c. 618 – 619); beat Shashanka of Gauda later
Banabhatta – Harshacharita, Kadambari; Harsha wrote Nagananda, Ratnavali, Priyadarshika
Kannauj (643, Mahayana, Hiuen Tsang presided); Prayag – Mahamoksha Parishad every 5 years
Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) 629 – 645 – Si-yu-ki; studied at Nalanda

traps: Harsha lost to Pulakeshin II (Aihole inscription)

keys.name: Pallavas

rows.v: 600 – 630; Mattavilasa Prahasana; Vichitrachitta; rock-cut temples (Mandagapattu); Jain → Shaiva (Appar)
630 – 668; "Vatapikonda" – killed Pulakeshin II 642; Mahabalipuram rathas, Arjuna's Penance; Hiuen Tsang visited Kanchi
Early Pallava Prakrit grants found in Andhra (Mayidavolu, Hirahadagalli)

traps: Shore temple = Rajasimha; Pancha rathas = Narasimhavarman I

keys.name: Chalukyas of Badami

rows.v: 610 – 642; beat Harsha; took Vengi (brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana); embassy to Persia (Khusrau II, Ajanta painting); killed by Narasimhavarman I
Took Kanchi; queen Lokamahadevi built Virupaksha temple, Pattadakal
Aihole (Lad Khan, Durga), Badami caves, Pattadakal (UNESCO) – Nagara + Dravida

traps: Aihole inscription by Ravikirti = Pulakeshin II beating Harsha

rows.v: Sudas (Bharata, priest Vasishtha) beat 10 tribes (Vishvamitra's side)
Alexander won; Porus kept his land; army stopped at Beas
1.5 lakh taken, 1 lakh killed (Rock Edict XIII)
Dhamma-vijaya replaced war; Ashoka became Buddhist
Chandragupta Maurya vs Seleucus I Nicator
Treaty – Afghanistan, Baluchistan to Maurya; 500 elephants; marriage alliance; Megasthenes sent
Karikala Chola beat Cheras, Pandyas and 11 chiefs
Pulakeshin II won; Harsha's south push stopped
Narasimhavarman I Pallava (general Paranjothi) killed Pulakeshin II
Title "Vatapikonda"; Chalukyas back under Vikramaditya I

sheets.title: Ancient dynasties side by side
sheets.intro: Who ruled at the same time. Tap a bar to see its box.
